intro: Interpolation uses relative position inside a local interval, so irregular sample spacing matters. A query halfway in time receives halfway between the two neighboring values.
task: Interpolate queries on a strictly increasing grid with constant endpoint extension and preserved query order.
requirements: times is strictly increasing with length at least two; values has the same length. queries is a vector in arbitrary order.
Linearly interpolate between bracketing samples. For queries below or above the sampled domain, return the nearest endpoint value.
Return one numeric NumPy vector in query order. An exact sample time returns its sample value.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Locate the two sample times surrounding each query before forming a fraction.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Interpolate values with that fraction and handle outside-domain queries using endpoint extension.

explanation: Interpolation uses relative position inside a local interval, so irregular sample spacing matters. A query halfway in time receives halfway between the two neighboring values.
Endpoint extension is a separate modeling choice from interpolation. Making it explicit prevents accidental linear extrapolation beyond the measured domain.
